node.title: Re^2: Please help me understand string eval better
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
exactly as if you wrote this

I get the point you're trying to make and I made a very similar one in my post, but note that this part isn't accurate, since [doc://do] is different from [doc://eval] in that code run by [doc://do] can't see lexicals in the enclosing scope. Specifically:

use warnings; use strict; use Path::Tiny 'path'; my $var = \"09"; my $transf = "/3+6"; print eval('$$var'.$transf),"\n"; # prints 9 path('third')->spew('$$var'.$transf); print do('third'),"\n"; # prints 6

Because in the file third, neither [doc://warnings] or [doc://strict] are in effect and it can't see my $var, it's the same as undef()/3+6. (Of course if you s/my/our/g, it does work.)
